minutes.headline: School Committee approved the override-adjusted FY25 budget, with one member abstaining
minutes.summary: The committee finalized the FY25 budget as adjusted after the successful override, approved a $76,336 line-item transfer, and heard from a TMS consultant about ongoing MUNIS and accounting delays at Town Hall. It also debated the LHS activity fee's fairness, revisited the parent-teacher conference calendar, appointed a member to the town manager search committee, discussed a town payroll-timing change that could cause employees to miss a paycheck, and reviewed i-Ready assessment results showing strong K-5 progress and weaker middle-school results, before entering executive session.

votes.motion: Approve the March 6, 2024 and March 27, 2024 minutes with revisions
Approve line item transfers totaling $76,336 as proposed
Approve the school handbooks for next year
Approve the change in date for parent-teacher conferences at the primary and elementary schools from fall to January
Approve the payroll modifications for the unaffiliated salary schedule
Appoint Peter beardmore to the town manager hiring screening committee
Approve the revised school calendar for 2024-25
Have the chair write a letter regarding the ARPA funds
Approve the FY25 budget as presented at the stated total
Enter executive session and adjourn after

budget_items.what_was_said: The chair reported the warrant total for the period and asked if anyone had questions.

TMS consultant Paul Livingston explained a transfer moving money from psychologist salaries, fire safety and furniture repair lines to dues and fees, transportation, computer purchase/lease, and water charges, because psychologist positions could not be filled and a contracted service was used instead.
A one-year, 2.5% increase was proposed for unaffiliated staff, mostly extended-day program employees paid from a revolving account, with minimal budget impact.

All high school students pay a mandatory annual activity fee funding guest speakers, advisor stipends, Science Olympiad, graduation/homecoming supplies and some field trip bus costs; students who don't pay cannot graduate. The board discussed whether it is fair as a mandatory, non-optional fee.
Middle school clubs such as ski club and Science Olympiad charge a per-club fee covering supplies, registration and some transportation.
Turkey Hill charges a fee for after-school activities, funding teacher stipends and materials for a roughly five-week session.
The primary school charges a similar fee for its after-school activity sessions, funding stipends and materials.

The committee discussed returning ARPA funds to the town for reappropriation by the select board, consistent with what was represented at town meeting, and asked to be part of future discussions on how the money is reused.

budget_items.topic: Maintenance of buildings contracted services line
budget_items.what_was_said: This line was discussed relative to the prior year's figure and the current budget figure after removing E911 compliance costs intended to be funded through ARPA.
A one-time E911 compliance cost was discussed as possibly funded through ARPA or state earmark funds; there was uncertainty whether an earmark would come through.
A public safety training system fell just below the funding line on the capital plan; a member expressed support for finding a way to fund it.
The out-of-district/private special education tuition line was funded at a stated amount, adjusted based on newly known student needs.
This line was adjusted due to a transition between IEP software systems.
The curriculum adoption line was reduced as part of budget line adjustments.

budget_items.topic: Primary school math supplies / library books
budget_items.what_was_said: These lines were reduced after principals were told they could spend down current-year budget lines that had been frozen.
The special education transportation line was increased to reflect newly known added students requiring transportation.

The committee voted to approve the total budget reflecting the override, adjusted from the earlier 'pink' budget for updated salaries and grant offsets, with one member abstaining due to insufficient review time.

The chair reported Chapter 70 came in higher than expected for Lunenburg and said she needed to ask the state representative where the additional amount came from, given the district is not a hold-harmless district.

budget_items.topic: Town payroll timing change / overtime pay
budget_items.what_was_said: Members objected to a planned change in town payroll timing that could cause employees, including lower-wage workers, to miss a paycheck by about a week; they asked for cost details on mitigation options such as a special check.

transfers.description: From psychologist salaries, fire safety, and furniture repair lines to dues and fees, regular transportation, computer purchase and lease, and water charges
Anticipated future transfer from the salary reserve line to appropriate salary lines once collective bargaining contracts are settled

decisions.decision: The chair will reply to the state representative's office that someone from the committee will attend the DESE regional meeting regardless of who holds the chair role at that time.
The superintendent's office will develop the requested overview/talking points about the district for DESE.
Discussion of TMS's suggested best practices for financial operations will be held for a summer workshop rather than at this meeting.

The LHS activity fee and related fee structure will be revisited as a fall agenda item before the FY26 budget process begins, with the superintendent researching how other districts handle similar fees.
The committee will work to schedule the legislative delegation meeting for the fall rather than immediately, given the state budget process has largely concluded for this cycle.
The June 26th meeting will be held remotely via Zoom given member availability.

what_happened.line: The committee approved the override-adjusted FY25 budget, with one member abstaining.
Members approved a line-item transfer moving funds out of unfilled psychologist salary lines into other accounts.
A consultant reported ongoing MUNIS accounting delays at Town Hall affecting the district's financial operations.
The board put off a decision on the mandatory high school activity fee to a fall meeting, ahead of the FY26 budget process.
Members raised concern that a town payroll-timing change could cause employees to miss a paycheck; no resolution was reached.

why_it_matters: This vote finalizes the school budget funded by the property tax override residents approved, setting spending for the coming year.
The high school's mandatory activity fee -- required for graduation -- will be revisited before next year's budget is built, which could change what students and families pay.
A town-wide payroll timing change under discussion could affect when school district employees receive a paycheck.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree closely on the meeting's actual business — nearly every vote, the $76,336 transfer, and the FY25 budget total line up — but our minutes garble several names/roles via captions (chair vs. superintendent, "Mr Leighton"/"Mrs brazowski"+"Laura" for Brian Lehtinen and Laura Brzozoski, "town manager" vs. "town accountant" screening committee) and add two things the official record does not support: an abstention on the FY25 budget vote (official says "all approve") and a standalone "payroll modifications" vote where the official minutes show no vote was taken and members actively disagreed with the change.
